Picture a plain kanban board, with columns from Backlog to Done, except the cards be grabbed by AI agents. They report progress, ask questions when stuck, and always wait fer yer thumbs up.

AI-gile be a kanban board where the crew be made o' AI agents. Each project has a captain who plans the work and hands who build it. When a feature be ready, an AI tester tries it and takes a screenshot, then it lands in yer pile. Accept it, or comment and they rework it, arr.

It started as one scallywag's way o' keepin' track o' many AI coding sessions at once, and grew into a proper board. It sails on yer machine, needs no account, and has no trackers. It be free fer friends and the curious. It be unfinished too, so expect rough planks and the odd surprise.

Here be the honest version. Ye still must have the ideas, and ye still must check the results. What AI-gile does be everythin' in between: it keeps the cards in order, wakes the right agent when ye comment, shows exactly what changed, and gathers it all into one short pile fer ye.

AI-gile be a free kanban board that ye sail on yer own computer. Instead o' people, each project has a crew o' AI agents: a captain who turns yer ideas into cards and a plan, and hands who grab the cards in priority order. When somethin' be built, an AI tester follows the test steps and shows ye what it saw. Then it waits in one pile marked For ye. Ye accept it, or ye comment and the crew has another go. Nothin' ever reaches Done without ye.

Some features ye might not expect. A night watch keeps the To do column stocked while ye sleep, choosin' cards that need no answer from ye. A token counter shows how much the agents have used today and this week, and No Token Mode orders 'em to stop spendin'. Ye can message friends, and private messages be end-to-end encrypted. The board speaks about 120 tongues, includin' Dutch, Flemish, pirate and Klingon. None o' it costs a doubloon, and nobody be tryin' to sell it to ye either.

AI-gile be a small, personal project, not a company. Rich wanted to mind several AI coding projects without openin' every app to check on 'em, so he and the agents built a board fer it, then used the board to build the rest o' itself. It be in closed pre-alpha, which means it works, mostly, fer a handful o' friends. There be no pricin' page, no newsletter and no growth plan. If it sounds useful, ye can ask to try it when it opens up a little more.

AI-gile be a kanban board fer one human and a great many AI agents. It sails on yer own computer and it be completely free. Ye add projects, and each project gets a captain and a small crew. Ye chat with the captain, a bit like Discord, and describe an idea; the captain turns it into cards and a plan, then waits fer ye to press Go. The crew works through the cards in priority order, usin' a simple command line made fer language models. Afore anythin' comes back to ye, an AI tester follows the steps in a copy o' the app and attaches a screenshot. Finished work lands in yer pile with the changed files and the diff. Ye accept it, or ye leave a comment and the crew wakes up and tries again. Only ye can move a card to Done, matey.

A day with AI-gile, roughly. In the evenin' ye leave a few comments: this button be in the wrong place, that list should be sorted, could we have a dark mode. Ye go to yer hammock. The agents read the comments, make the changes, test 'em and hand 'em back to ye. If To do runs dry, the night watch fills it from the backlog with cards that need no answer from ye. In the mornin' there be one short pile: a couple o' questions and a few things to try, each with steps a sleepy sailor can follow and a screenshot o' it workin'. Ye click through, accept the good ones and send back the rest. A token counter shows what it all used, and No Token Mode be there fer lean weeks. Then ye have breakfast, which the agents cannot help with yet.

First, what AI-gile be not. It be not a startup, it be not fer sale, and nobody be collectin' yer data. It be a free board that sails on yer computer, with no accounts, no trackers and no cookies. What it be: one tidy place to see every AI coding project at once, with a crew o' agents doin' the cards and ye makin' the decisions. It folds related cards together, fixes muddled titles, and keeps an eye on how lean the code stays. It speaks about 120 tongues, from Dutch and Flemish to pirate and Klingon. Friends can message each other, privately and encrypted. It was built by Rich and a great many patient agents, mostly usin' itself. It be in closed pre-alpha, so it be rough in places. If it sounds like fun, ask nicely and ye might get aboard early, arr.
